$comment: Speaker-notes cue vocabulary, the single source. Read by scripts/notes-lint.ts (undocumented tag = hard fail) and pointed to by SlideCraft References/SpeakerNotesCues.md. A tag is the upper-case word or words that open a bracket at the start of a notes line; what follows inside the bracket (a duration, a count, a condition after a colon, a lower-case qualifier) is not part of the name. Several tags may share one bracket separated by commas. Grammar and registers: SpeakerNotesCues.md. Add a tag here on its second use across decks.

grammar.line: - [TAG] cue in spoken syntax, 3 to 8 words
grammar.suffix: - [TAG 90s] duration or count as a plain suffix
grammar.verbatim: - [VERBATIM] "the exact sentence, sentence case, no caps inside"

PAUSE.means: stop talking, let it land, then advance; a duration may follow

SLOW.means: the next line is spoken slower than the rest

POINT.means: point at the slide element the cue names

CLICK.means: this slide has N fragment builds; the cues that follow are one per click

VERBATIM.means: quoted line said word for word; wording is the payload

MEMORIZED.means: scripted open or close, rehearsed from SCRIPT.md; notes carry the first spoken line and the beats

ABORT.means: one fallback per failure mode of an interactive element; the condition follows a colon

BRIDGE.means: the one transition sentence, last bullet, only where the join is unnatural

extension.EYES UP: do not look down at all on this slide; the room is voting, playing or answering
extension.HARD STOP: the clock time the talk must end; on the Q&A slide and in the slide 1 pre-show block
extension.READ: a figure, name or quote to be read exactly; full length, max 3 per slide
extension.SILENT: someone else is speaking (co-host, video); the speaker says nothing
extension.CHAT: ask the room to answer in the chat; the question follows in quotes
extension.CALLBACK: repeat an earlier line or image on purpose; name the slide it echoes
extension.PLANT: say something now that a later slide pays off
extension.PIVOT: the argument turns here; change tone
extension.BREATHE: a deliberate breath before a hard line
extension.RHETORICAL: a question the room is not expected to answer
extension.FRAME: why this matters to this audience, one line
extension.WAIT ROOM: hold until the room reacts (laugh, hands, votes) before continuing
extension.BADGE GREEN?: slide 1 pre-show check of the poll freshness badge in speaker view

namedSlot.$comment: [RONALD 30s] style: a named co-presenter and their slot, a stage direction rather than an attribution. NAME is replaced by the upper-cased co-presenter names the lint is given (--copresenters); matched against the whole bracket part.

prepPrefixes.$comment: Lines that belong to the slide 1 pre-show block only; anywhere else they are prep leakage (hard fail). Matched at the start of the line after the bullet marker, case-sensitive, brackets optional.
